Jordan / Kimberly,

Thanks for the note and the attachments — useful. A few clarifying questions from Helios legal before we proceed to DocuSign:

1) TIA vs DTIA: can you confirm whether Redwood will provide a summarized Technical Impact Assessment (TIA) that maps data flows and the cryptographic protections (KMS key custody, algorithmic details) or whether Helios should expect a DTIA (detailed developer-level version) as well? Our security team will want the TIA high level and the DTIA on an as-needed inspection basis.

2) HSM / KMS: the tech-evidence-manifest references a keystore attestation — can Redwood confirm: (a) where KMS keys are held (cloud provider region), (b) whether keys are customer- or provider-managed, and (c) whether you can provide an HSM attestation (redwood-kms-hsm-attest.pdf).

3) Residual risk / onshore fallback: the UK IDTA addendum language you proposed includes a fallback statement — is that an automatic failover (and therefore material change to the SLA), or an operational runbook? Helios needs that distinction so procurement can assess service credits exposure.

4) Evidence access: please point us to the secure location for the evidence package (SFTP or GDrive link with limited access will do).

If you can confirm the above and provide the HSM attestation, Helios is prepared to proceed with a signing window the week of Jan 25.

Best,
Elise

Elise / Helios legal team —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers here and pointers below.

1) TIA vs DTIA: Redwood will deliver a TIA (high-level mapping of data flows, retention pathways, and cryptographic controls) as part of the DPA package. The DTIA (detailed developer-level diagrams and logs) can be provided on a controlled-access basis under an evidentiary request and NDA; we typically stage DTIA access through our secure audit portal.

2) KMS / HSM: keys are customer-isolated within the cloud provider region you choose. By default keys are provider-managed but we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) for enterprise customers — that configuration is selectable in the onboarding sheet. Attached: redwood-kms-hsm-attest.pdf (attestation) and tech-evidence-manifest.csv. Summary:
- Key regions: eu-west-1 (Ireland) for EU/UK workloads;
- Default custody: Redwood-managed (but CMK option available);
- HSM attestation: Provided (see attachment).

3) Onshore fallback: the fallback we describe is operational — an automated routing policy that prefers onshore cache for EU/UK-labeled requests and fails over to the designated onshore node. It does not create a separate SLA credit entitling Helios to financial remediation by default. If Helios requires a contractually-backed SLA change (i.e., explicit credits tied to residency failover), we can scope that as an add-on and surface estimated cost.

4) Evidence access: we’ve staged the artifacts in a secure workspace. Link (limited access): https://drive.redwood.ai/Helios/transfer-evidence/manifest. Credentials/access audit will be recorded.

Next steps I recommend:
- Jordan to confirm signing window (DocuSign send) and procurement PO expectations.
- Marissa to prepare a final redline that stitches the UK IDTA as Schedule B and confirms the fallback language phrasing.
